transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Meeting title: Redwood Inference x AWS Marketplace — listing refresh requirements + security attachments
Date: Jan 14, 2026
Time: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: 43:12
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees:
- Talia Benson (Redwood Inference)
- Soojin Lee (Redwood Inference)
- Marcus Lin (Redwood Inference)
- Ethan Park (Redwood Inference)
- Elliot Price (Redwood Inference)
- Megan O’Connell (AWS Marketplace)
- Rajiv Nair (AWS Marketplace)


Summary (auto-generated):
Redwood reviewed required AWS Marketplace listing fields and attachments for the upcoming listing refresh. AWS clarified security/compliance claim boundaries, what evidence can be attached vs provided under NDA, and typical review timelines. Redwood aligned on submitting updated copy, screenshots, support contacts, and a concise security packet with accurate encryption/audit logging language.

Topics:
- AWS Marketplace SaaS listing fields (headline, highlights, categories, pricing notes)
- SKU structure and how to represent add-ons (compliance/retention/SLA)
- Security documentation requirements (SOC 2 handling, encryption, audit logs, incident response)
- Submission deadlines and review lead times
- Common rejection reasons (over-claims, broken links, screenshot issues)

Action items:
- Talia Benson — consolidate copy + attachment list into one submission checklist and share with AWS — Due Jan 20
- Soojin Lee — finalize “Highlights” bullets and keyword set per AWS limits — Due Jan 20
- Marcus Lin — review security packet wording for audit logging / KMS / retention claims — Due Jan 19
- Elliot Price — deliver updated screenshots and confirm docs URLs are stable (no redirects/broken anchors) — Due Jan 22
- Megan O’Connell — confirm preferred attachment format and if SOC 2 can be referenced without uploading the report — Due Jan 18


Transcript:

[00:00:03] Megan O’Connell: Alright, I think we’re recording now. Hi everyone. Thanks for making time. The goal today is to make sure you know what Marketplace needs for the refresh so we don’t get stuck in a back-and-forth during review.

[00:00:16] Talia Benson: Perfect. Thanks Megan. Yeah, we’re trying to hit end of month for submission, so this is really helpful.

[00:00:24] Soojin Lee: Hi, I’m Soojin, product marketing. I own the listing copy and the attachments narrative.

[00:00:29] Marcus Lin: Marcus, security engineering. I’m here mostly to keep us honest on wording.

[00:00:34] Rajiv Nair: Hey all, Rajiv here. I cover technical validation for a lot of the SaaS listings, especially when there’s webhook-based provisioning and entitlements.

[00:00:43] Megan O’Connell: Great. So first, just to level set: you’re a SaaS contract listing today, correct?

[00:00:49] Talia Benson: Yes, SaaS contract. We’re not doing an AMI. The purchase triggers entitlements on our side and then the customer links their AWS account to a Redwood org in our console.

[00:01:00] Rajiv Nair: Okay. That’s the right mental model. Where people get tripped up is if the “how to get started” section doesn’t clearly explain the account linking step and how long entitlements can take.

[00:01:12] Elliot Price: That’s exactly what we’re updating in docs. Our current page is a bit vague.

[00:01:18] Megan O’Connell: Cool. So listing requirements — I’ll just walk through common required fields and the “gotchas” we see.

[00:01:25] Megan O’Connell: For the public listing page, the Marketplace team will look at: headline, short description, long description, at least three highlights, categories, and support information. You’d be surprised how many get rejected because the support URL goes to a login wall.

[00:01:41] Soojin Lee: Noted. Our docs are public, but our console is of course logged in. We’ll make sure support and onboarding docs are public.

[00:01:48] Megan O’Connell: Exactly. Also: you need a support email that’s monitored. A shared alias is fine. And then an SLA statement — it can be “best effort” if that’s your model, but it needs to be consistent with any claims in the copy.

[00:02:02] Talia Benson: We have premium SLAs for dedicated capacity, but Hosted is more standard. For Marketplace SKUs, we have an add-on called Premium SLA. We were debating whether that’s a separate line item or described as a plan level.

[00:02:17] Megan O’Connell: Yeah, so Marketplace is flexible, but avoid describing an “add-on” if it’s not purchasable as a dimension in the product. If you’re doing separate SKUs for add-ons, make that explicit and consistent.

[00:02:31] Rajiv Nair: And operationally, make sure your fulfillment can detect what was purchased. If you say “premium SLA includes faster support response,” you need a way to map that to an entitlement on your side.

[00:02:42] Ethan Park: We do. We’re building a mapping layer — AWS SKU ID to an internal entitlement ID. Then the console shows “active entitlements” in the org billing page.

[00:02:54] Rajiv Nair: Perfect. That’s the right pattern.

[00:02:57] Megan O’Connell: Next: screenshots. Marketplace reviewers will check that screenshots match the product and don’t include sensitive customer data. If there are account IDs or emails, blur them.

[00:03:11] Elliot Price: Yep. We have a screenshot inventory and we’re using a demo tenant. I’ll double-check we don’t leak any internal IDs.

[00:03:20] Soojin Lee: We had a question on how many screenshots are recommended.

[00:03:23] Megan O’Connell: There’s no strict number, but we see best results with 3 to 6. One should show the onboarding step or setup flow. One can show usage analytics or whatever “value” page exists. Just don’t overwhelm.

[00:03:38] Talia Benson: Makes sense.

[00:03:41] Megan O’Connell: Now the big one: security and compliance attachments. For enterprise buyers, having a concise security overview PDF is helpful, but Marketplace reviewers will mostly care that you do not over-claim in the public listing.

[00:03:56] Marcus Lin: That’s our main concern. What’s acceptable language for SOC 2? We’re SOC 2 Type II, but we don’t want to upload the full report publicly.

[00:04:05] Megan O’Connell: Right. You should not upload your full SOC report as a public attachment. Most partners just say “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA upon request.” That’s generally acceptable.

[00:04:17] Rajiv Nair: Also avoid saying “AWS certified” unless it’s a specific program. People write “AWS certified secure” and it triggers review comments.

[00:04:25] Soojin Lee: Got it. We’ll stick to factual statements: SOC 2 Type II, encryption in transit and at rest, audit logs, and then “details available under NDA.”

[00:04:37] Marcus Lin: On encryption at rest — we use cloud provider managed encryption for storage, and we support customer-managed keys for some deployments, specifically Private in VPC. Hosted is encrypted, but not always CMK. We want to be precise.

[00:04:53] Rajiv Nair: That nuance is important. If you say “customer-managed keys for all data,” reviewers will ask how. You can say “encryption at rest using cloud-provider key management; customer-managed keys supported for Private/VPC deployments.”

[00:05:10] Marcus Lin: Perfect. That’s basically what we want.

[00:05:13] Megan O’Connell: The other one that gets flagged is “no data stored” or “we don’t retain prompts.” Unless that is literally true in all scenarios, don’t write it.

[00:05:24] Soojin Lee: We do have configurable retention windows, and we keep logs for reliability and billing. We’re trying to message it as “data retention is limited and configurable,” but we’ve had lots of debate.

[00:05:36] Marcus Lin: And we need to caveat that some logs exist for security and operations.

[00:05:40] Megan O’Connell: Right. A safe phrasing is “We retain data necessary to operate the service; retention periods vary by product and can be configured for eligible plans.” Something like that.

[00:05:52] Ethan Park: Are we required to provide an incident response plan as an attachment?

[00:05:57] Megan O’Connell: Not required for the listing review, but enterprise customers will ask. You can include a one-page “Security overview” that mentions you have an IR program and how to request details.

[00:06:09] Rajiv Nair: For Marketplace, the reviewer will check that you have a privacy policy link, terms/EULA, and that you’re not claiming things like “HIPAA compliant” if it’s not in a program.

[00:06:23] Soojin Lee: We’re not going to claim HIPAA. We do have customers in regulated industries though, so we talk about “supports regulated workloads,” which might be too vague.

[00:06:34] Megan O’Connell: “Supports regulated workloads” is okay if you define it as capabilities: VPC deployment, audit logging, encryption, access controls. Just don’t imply certification.

[00:06:45] Marcus Lin: Great. On audit logs, we have audit logs in Private and in Hosted for certain events (org membership changes, API key changes, SSO events). But not every inference request is an “audit event.”

[00:06:59] Rajiv Nair: Exactly. Don’t say “full audit logging of all inference traffic.” Say “administrative audit logs” or “security-relevant events.”

[00:07:09] Marcus Lin: That’s helpful. I’ll update our draft language.

[00:07:13] Talia Benson: Can we talk about the actual submission timeline? We were told review can take like two weeks.

[00:07:19] Megan O’Connell: Typical is 10 to 15 business days, assuming no major issues. If it’s a refresh to an existing listing, sometimes it’s faster, but I’d plan for two weeks.

[00:07:31] Talia Benson: So if we want it live by mid-Feb, we should submit by end of Jan.

[00:07:36] Megan O’Connell: Correct. Also note: late January gets busy because a lot of partners push updates. So earlier is better.

[00:07:45] Soojin Lee: What are the most common reasons for rejection in the review?

[00:07:50] Megan O’Connell: Number one is broken links. Number two is over-claims in security. Number three is unclear fulfillment instructions — like “subscribe and start using,” but there’s no step-by-step setup.

[00:08:04] Rajiv Nair: For SaaS, the reviewer often tests “subscribe” and expects either an immediate redirect to your onboarding or a clear email flow. If the user lands somewhere with no clue what to do, it’s a problem.

[00:08:17] Elliot Price: We’re adding an onboarding wizard in-console that detects a Marketplace entitlement and prompts for linking.

[00:08:23] Rajiv Nair: That will help a lot.

[00:08:26] Talia Benson: One question on entitlement delays. Sometimes AWS events take a bit. Are we expected to message a specific SLA like “within X minutes”?

[00:08:36] Rajiv Nair: Not required, but be transparent. Saying “usually within a few minutes; occasionally up to an hour” is better than promising “instant.”

[00:08:46] Marcus Lin: From security side, we also want to mention we validate webhook signatures and log events. But again, don’t want to overstate.

[00:08:55] Rajiv Nair: You can say “Marketplace events are validated and audited.” That’s okay. If you say “tamper-proof,” people will ask for details.

[00:09:04] Marcus Lin: Understood.

[00:09:07] Megan O’Connell: Another thing: If you attach a security packet, keep it short. Like 5 to 10 pages. Buyers want a narrative; detailed evidence is usually under NDA.

[00:09:17] Soojin Lee: Ours is currently… a little long. It’s like 18 pages including diagrams.

[00:09:22] Megan O’Connell: That’s not terrible, but try to separate “overview” versus “appendix.” The overview can be attached; the appendix can be “available upon request.”

[00:09:33] Ethan Park: For the listing itself, are we required to specify regions we operate in? We have multi-region, and for Dedicated/Private it depends.

[00:09:43] Rajiv Nair: For the listing, yes, at least for the SaaS fulfillment you should specify supported regions and any constraints. If a customer is in, say, eu-west-1 and your service only onboards in us-east-1, you want to avoid confusion.

[00:09:57] Talia Benson: We do support EU regions for Hosted, and Private is customer-specific. We can say “availability depends on deployment type.”

[00:10:05] Megan O’Connell: That’s fine. Just keep it clear.

[00:10:09] Soojin Lee: Can we ask about how to represent pricing? AWS doesn’t love external pricing tables, right?

[00:10:16] Megan O’Connell: Correct. You can describe “usage-based” or “contract” in general terms, but don’t put a table that conflicts with Marketplace pricing. If you want a calculator, it should be clearly labeled as an estimate.

[00:10:29] Talia Benson: We’re doing contract SKUs aligned to Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private. Dedicated and Private are more sales-assisted anyway.

[00:10:39] Rajiv Nair: Just ensure your dimensions are set properly. If Private is not self-serve, your “How to get started” should say “subscribe then contact vendor” or similar, and provide the process.

[00:10:53] Soojin Lee: That’s helpful. Our worry is losing the developer-first vibe.

[00:10:58] Megan O’Connell: You can keep it developer-first. Just add a procurement-friendly section: “If you need invoice/PO, here’s how Marketplace works.” That helps enterprise.

[00:11:09] Talia Benson: Yeah, we’re also building a customer FAQ.

[00:11:12] Megan O’Connell: Perfect.

[00:11:15] Rajiv Nair: I want to drill into one technical thing — your account linking. Is it AWS account ID to Redwood org? Or is it AWS subscription ID?

[00:11:25] Ethan Park: Both. We receive the Marketplace entitlement and the customer identifier. We store the Marketplace customer ID and map it to the Redwood org ID during linking. We also keep the AWS account ID for display and troubleshooting.

[00:11:39] Rajiv Nair: Great. Make sure the docs mention what identifier the customer needs to provide. Customers get confused between account ID, payer ID, subscription ID, all that.

[00:11:51] Elliot Price: We can add a screenshot of where to find it in AWS.

[00:11:55] Megan O’Connell: That’s a great idea.

[00:11:58] Soojin Lee: On copy compliance — are there any restricted terms we should avoid?

[00:12:05] Megan O’Connell: “Guaranteed” anything. “Compliant with” specific standards unless you are. “Military-grade.” Also, avoid mentioning other providers’ trademarks in a comparative way. You can say “works with popular models,” but don’t say “better than Bedrock” or something.

[00:12:22] Soojin Lee: Understood.

[00:12:25] Talia Benson: (laughs) No “military grade,” got it.

[00:12:28] Marcus Lin: We sometimes say “end-to-end encryption.” That can be misinterpreted. We should say “encryption in transit via TLS” and “encryption at rest.”

[00:12:37] Megan O’Connell: Yes. “End-to-end encryption” is risky because people think client-side keys.

[00:12:44] Rajiv Nair: Another detail: if you mention SSO/SAML, make sure it’s accurate and not “coming soon.” Reviewers might ask if it’s available to all plans.

[00:12:55] Marcus Lin: It’s available for enterprise tiers. We’ll say “SAML SSO available on eligible plans.”

[00:13:02] Megan O’Connell: Great.

[00:13:05] Talia Benson: Megan, can you confirm what you want as “attachments” in the partner portal for the refresh? We were thinking: a security overview PDF, architecture diagram, and a “getting started” PDF. Or is that too much.

[00:13:20] Megan O’Connell: That’s fine. But don’t attach duplicates. If your getting started is in docs, just link it. Attachments should be durable. And keep them updated — reviewers sometimes check the last updated date.

[00:13:35] Elliot Price: We can embed the “getting started” in docs and only attach the security PDF and architecture diagram.

[00:13:41] Megan O’Connell: That’s my recommendation.

[00:13:44] Rajiv Nair: And keep the architecture diagram simple — show data flow at a high level. Customers love it. Reviewers don’t need every microservice.

[00:13:55] Ethan Park: Good, because our internal diagram is… messy.

[00:13:59] (crosstalk)

[00:14:00] Soojin Lee: We’ll do a cleaned version.

[00:14:03] Marcus Lin: We’ll also need to ensure it matches reality.

[00:14:06] Megan O’Connell: Exactly.

[00:14:08] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s talk deadlines. If we target Jan 27 submission, is that reasonable?

[00:14:15] Megan O’Connell: Yes. If you can get it in by Jan 24 even better. But Jan 27 still gives you a shot for mid-Feb.

[00:14:25] Soojin Lee: What about the “change log” part? Do we need to provide a change summary in submission?

[00:14:31] Megan O’Connell: It’s helpful. Just a short bullet list: updated SKU naming, updated security attachments, improved onboarding instructions, updated screenshots.

[00:14:43] Talia Benson: Great.

[00:14:45] Rajiv Nair: Quick note: If you’re adding new dimensions/SKUs, you may need additional validation. That’s not just “copy refresh.” So account for that. Sometimes it’s basically a mini-launch.

[00:14:58] Talia Benson: That’s a good point. We are adding add-on SKUs.

[00:15:02] Megan O’Connell: Yeah. We’ll treat it as a substantive update, not just text changes.

[00:15:08] Marcus Lin: For security evidence, is a pen test attestation letter okay as an attachment?

[00:15:14] Megan O’Connell: You can attach an executive summary or attestation letter, as long as it doesn’t include sensitive details. Many partners do.

[00:15:23] Marcus Lin: Our pen test vendor provides a short letter. We’ll include that.

[00:15:27] Rajiv Nair: Again, avoid dates that look stale. If it’s from 2022, it may raise questions.

[00:15:34] Marcus Lin: Ours is recent.

[00:15:36] Megan O’Connell: Great.

[00:15:38] Soojin Lee: We also want to add a “Shared Responsibility” section. Does AWS have any preferred wording?

[00:15:46] Megan O’Connell: No strict template, but keep it simple: what AWS secures, what you secure, what the customer is responsible for in configuration.

[00:15:57] Ethan Park: For example, for Private in customer VPC, customer manages network controls and access. For Hosted, we manage infra.

[00:16:04] Megan O’Connell: Exactly.

[00:16:06] Rajiv Nair: One more thing: if you mention data residency, be careful. “We support EU data residency” should mean the data actually stays in EU regions as configured.

[00:16:18] Marcus Lin: For Hosted, customers can select region for processing. We still have some global control plane logs. So we need to be careful.

[00:16:26] Rajiv Nair: Yep. Then say “inference processing region selection” rather than absolute residency.

[00:16:34] Soojin Lee: That’s a really good catch.

[00:16:37] Talia Benson: Okay, maybe we should do a quick pass through the copy and see if there are any red flags now.

[00:16:44] Megan O’Connell: Sure, read me your headline and top highlights.

[00:16:48] Soojin Lee: Headline draft: “Redwood Inference — high-performance LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”

[00:16:56] Megan O’Connell: That’s fine.

[00:16:58] Soojin Lee: Highlights: “Lower latency and cost via optimized serving runtime.” “Deployment flexibility: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, VPC/on-prem.” “Enterprise controls: SSO, audit logs, encryption, and configurable retention.”

[00:17:13] Rajiv Nair: The third highlight is okay but add “on eligible plans” for SSO and retention if it’s not universal.

[00:17:21] Marcus Lin: Agreed.

[00:17:23] Megan O’Connell: And “on-prem” can be okay, just make sure you actually deliver that as part of Private offering.

[00:17:30] Talia Benson: We do, but it’s not via Marketplace self-serve. It’s sales-assisted.

[00:17:36] Megan O’Connell: That’s okay, just set expectations.

[00:17:39] Soojin Lee: In the long description, we mention “SOC 2” and “ISO.” We are ISO 27001 in progress, not certified.

[00:17:48] Marcus Lin: Yeah, we should remove ISO mention or phrase as “aligns with ISO 27001 controls,” but that can also be risky.

[00:17:56] Megan O’Connell: I would not mention ISO unless you are certified. It’s just not worth the review ping.

[00:18:03] Soojin Lee: Okay, we’ll drop it.

[00:18:06] Talia Benson: Great.

[00:18:08] Rajiv Nair: On the onboarding steps, you should include something like:
1) Subscribe in AWS Marketplace.
2) Wait for entitlement activation (usually minutes).
3) Create or sign in to Redwood.
4) Link AWS Marketplace subscription to your Redwood org.
5) Generate an API key and test.

[00:18:28] Elliot Price: That is basically what we’re drafting.

[00:18:31] Megan O’Connell: Perfect.

[00:18:33] Talia Benson: One more question: Are there any requirements around refund policy language?

[00:18:39] Megan O’Connell: For SaaS contract, you should state your refund/cancellation policy. Many partners say “No refunds for partial months” or “case-by-case.” Just be consistent with your legal terms.

[00:18:53] Talia Benson: Okay. We’ll confirm with legal.

[00:18:56] Marcus Lin: Also any requirements around storing customer data? Like privacy policy link is required, right.

[00:19:02] Megan O’Connell: Yes. Privacy policy is required. And make sure it clearly states what data you collect and how it’s used.

[00:19:10] Soojin Lee: Our privacy policy is public. We’ll also add a marketplace-specific FAQ.

[00:19:15] Rajiv Nair: Good. A marketplace FAQ reduces support tickets.

[00:19:20] Talia Benson: Okay, I think we’re good. Megan, can you send us the checklist you referenced?

[00:19:26] Megan O’Connell: Yes, I’ll send the Marketplace listing refresh checklist and the security claims guidance doc. It’s not long.

[00:19:33] Talia Benson: Great.

[00:19:35] (brief silence)

[00:19:37] Soojin Lee: Rajiv, for the “technical validation,” do we need to provide test credentials or a demo environment?

[00:19:44] Rajiv Nair: Usually no for SaaS contract, but reviewers may try your onboarding. If it requires an invite, that can be an issue. Ideally, anyone can create a Redwood account and see the “link subscription” flow.

[00:19:59] Ethan Park: Yes, it’s open sign-up. The linking requires the AWS customer ID, which is only present after subscription.

[00:20:06] Rajiv Nair: That’s fine.

[00:20:08] Marcus Lin: And if a customer is trying to link and they’re in the wrong region — we’ve had that. We’re improving error messaging.

[00:20:16] Rajiv Nair: Great. Also include a troubleshooting section: “If you don’t see entitlement after X minutes, contact support with your AWS Marketplace customer ID.”

[00:20:28] Elliot Price: We’ll do that.

[00:20:31] Megan O’Connell: Okay, last thing: submission packaging. When you submit, include:
- updated long description
- highlights
- categories and keywords
- updated screenshots
- support contacts
- attachment(s) like security overview and architecture diagram
- short change summary

[00:20:53] Talia Benson: Got it.

[00:20:55] Megan O’Connell: And please, please double-check that every link is accessible without logging in. That’s always the dumb reason things get delayed.

[00:21:05] Talia Benson: We will. Elliot, you’re on that.

[00:21:08] Elliot Price: I’m on it.

[00:21:10] Soojin Lee: Thank you both.

[00:21:12] Megan O’Connell: Great. I’ll send the docs today. Can we tentatively plan a quick check-in next week?

[00:21:18] Talia Benson: Yes, I’ll send a hold for next Wednesday.

[00:21:22] Megan O’Connell: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

[00:21:24] Rajiv Nair: Thanks.

[00:21:25] (call ends)

Note: Fireflies transcription may contain errors in proper nouns and technical terms.
